title: The Old Gravestone (The Memory of Goodness)
summary: An ancient gravestone had been moved to the kitchen courtyard to serve as a stepping stone by the well. Its inscription was nearly worn away by the footsteps of water-carriers....
full_text:
An ancient gravestone had been moved to the kitchen courtyard to serve as a stepping stone by the well. Its inscription was nearly worn away by the footsteps of water-carriers.

Yet an aged woman looked upon the worn stone and recounted the life of the merchant who lay buried beneath its original site: his open granaries during the plague, his rescue of stranded sailors, and his daily gifts of bread to the blind.

The children knelt upon the stone and traced the worn names with reverent fingers, realizing that human love is inscribed upon the living tablets of eternity.
moral: The memory of the righteous is blessed; quiet acts of mercy survive the decay of marble.
